VM sweep (A3): from 16:33 to 16:36 UTC on 2026-10-30 another team's test of an unmerged runner change destroyed every Ubicloud VM in the project named without an expiry and older than 4 hours, 22 F6 VMs among them (S1 gbrain c0 to c9, S1 temporal graph c0 to c9, the S1 file agent and D8 graph pipeline c9). A3 relaunched S1 gbrain c0 to c9, S1 temporal graph c0 to c3 and D8 graph pipeline c9 from fresh stores, with VM names that carry an expiry and a watcher that saves each unit's spend every 30 minutes; A4 and A4b ran the rest.

Rows reused from Q1's A24 campaign (q1-scoreboard-sealed, launch commit 008b83fe) for ext-extract-first, ext-memory-bank, ext-graph-pipeline, ext-markdown-kb, ext-verbatim-session, baseline-none, baseline-recency and baseline-full-context, each declared in the F6 preregistration and passing eval/runner/q1/reuse-check.ts from 008b83fe to d9fffb93. baseline-hybrid and baseline-file-agent fail that check, so their S1 rows were rerun at the F6 tree and their S2b, S2a and S3 rows are not run. ext-temporal-graph's A24 rows were retired (its pinned configuration calls models its provider retired); F6 measures its 0.31.2 shipped defaults instead (configuration shipped-0.31).

S1 is descriptive and unranked: with 10 conversations Q1's power check detects only differences of about 13.6 points, so no S1 row leads, beats or trails another. Arm P is gbrain's headline row on every set; arms A0, A, B, C, D and E are measurements beside it. D8 is published here descriptively.

D8 confirmatory family (preregistered; computed in custody from the receipt's canonical judgments by the procedure the preregistration names, since eval/runner/scoreboard.ts does not compute it): on claude-sonnet-5-5's paired correct/incorrect over 300 questions (canonical score >= 0.5), (1) the facts block P - A is +1.33 points (92.00% vs 90.67%; 12 wins, 8 losses; exact McNemar p = 0.503; question-level paired bootstrap 95% interval -1.67 to +4.33, conversation-cluster interval -2.67 to +6.33); (2) the full stack D - A is +0.33 points (13 wins, 12 losses; p = 1.0; interval -3.00 to +3.67); (3) recall B - A is 0.00 points (10 wins, 10 losses; p = 1.0; interval -3.00 to +3.00). Holm-adjusted p is 1.0 for all three, so none passes at 0.05, and "the facts block helps on D8" is not written: on these fresh long histories the facts block did not measurably change accuracy. Opus 5.5 (P - A +1.00, 20 wins, 17 losses) and gpt-6.1-sol (+0.67, 15 wins, 13 losses) agree. Arm A already answers about 9 in 10 correctly for every reader, which limits the room any arm has to gain; the facts block was delivered (about 85% of P's contexts carry fact items, about 15 per context).

S1 file agent (A5): like the S1 hybrid, the A4 unit ran Q1's definition of its cell id, and its receipt is merged and published under that definition, as it ran. The two definitions have the same questions, readers, agent mode and canonical judge; Q1's also asks for frontier judges, ten judge repeats and 20 ingest-latency probes. F6's comparison reads only the canonical judge (judge_replicate 0), so it is what F6's definition would have produced; the extra work was paid inside the $3,100 cap. The cell runner now refuses an id both manifests define unless --manifest names one.

S1 gbrain (A3): two of the ten conversations (shards c8 and c9) ingested degraded: gbrain's F6 build refused its own /finish because 2 and 3 pages were skipped as unparsed (pages_skipped_unparsed), the product's own failure, not a harness budget. Their 40 questions were answered from those stores and are scored, as every ingest_degraded answer is, so the headline row keeps them; the sensitivity view f6-s1-gbrain-degraded-ingest reads every system without those 40 questions.

Arm B recall (added 2026-11-03, after publication; #343): arm B is the only gbrain arm that retrieves with gbrain's `recall`, so this note covers its rows alone: S1 `s1.gbrain-defaults.f6-master.b`, S2b `s2b.gbrain-defaults.f6-master.b` and D8 arm B, including D8's B - A comparison, plus the partial A1 appendix rows S2a `s2a.gbrain-defaults.f6-master.b` and S3 `s3.gbrain-defaults.f6-master.b`, from which no comparison is drawn. At the pin, `recall` reports degradation in its response (`facts_degraded`, `search_degraded` and delivery fallbacks), but the gbrain-defaults shim classified every recall response as scored, and neither the shim nor the runner kept that response metadata. A silently degraded recall would therefore score as a miss rather than be retried, and whether any did was not measured. Keyword-only page search is ruled out, because the same serves' query arm ran with vectors; facts that had no embedding at query time are not ruled out. The headline arm P and the D8 P - A comparison retrieve with `query`, not `recall`, and are unaffected. No arm-B number is changed.

S1 file agent block label (added 2026-11-04, after publication): the S1 file-agent row's receipt names block T1, Q1's S1 headline block, because the A4 unit ran without `--manifest f6` (see the A5 note above). Its run configuration, `cells/s1.baseline-file-agent.baseline.whole-agent/run-config.json` (sha256 `07b938b4`, listed under Inputs), is the one this scoreboard publishes, and it tells the row apart from Q1's own cell of that id. So this is a label fix, not a re-run: the row's rows, answers and judgments hash as before. The particle-1 add-on pairs its file-agent row with this cell by that run configuration (`F6_FILE_AGENT_CONFIG_SHA256` in eval/runner/q1/particle-addon-report.ts).
